projects.name: Oja Ledger
projects.summary: Offline double-entry bookkeeping for Nigerian traders. Record a sale in two taps with no network, then get profit, VAT returns and the small-company tax check under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025.
projects.hardestPart: Every entry is sealed with a SHA-256 hash of the one before it, so editing any past naira is detectable. Money is whole kobo, never floats, and four ledger invariants are checked against 200 generated trading histories each on every push.

caseStudy.problem: A provisions seller in a Nigerian market may take 40 payments a day across cash, transfer and POS, sell on credit and restock weekly. At month end she can say roughly what came in, but not her profit, her VAT, or whether she qualifies for the 0% small-company tax rate. Existing tools assume reliable internet, a laptop and an accountant’s vocabulary. The goal: books that are correct by construction, kept on a phone, usable with no network, in plain language.

decisions.t: Real double-entry, hidden from the user
decisions.d: Every tap becomes a balanced journal entry over a small chart of accounts, so credit sales, VAT and owner drawings all work and a balance sheet is possible. The UI never says “debit”; an accountant can export everything as CSV.

decisions.t: Whole kobo, never floats
decisions.d: Every amount is an integer number of kobo behind a branded Kobo type, so TypeScript blocks a stray float. VAT is stored in basis points and split so net + VAT always equals the gross price.

decisions.t: Prove the rules with property-based tests
decisions.d: On every push, CI builds 200 random trading histories and asserts the trial balance balances, assets equal liabilities plus equity, reversals restore every account, and six kinds of tampering are caught.

decisions.t: Make tampering visible with a hash chain
decisions.d: Each entry stores a SHA-256 hash that includes the previous entry’s hash. Changing one naira in an old entry breaks every later link, and the app re-verifies the chain on open.

decisions.t: Append-only, with reversals
decisions.d: No edit and no delete. A mistake is fixed by a linked mirror-image entry and the original stays visible, crossed out, the way real accounting systems work.

decisions.t: Offline-first and atomic
decisions.d: The book lives in IndexedDB. Each save writes the entries and the new chain head in one transaction, and a service worker lets the app open with no network.

results: 29 automated tests in CI, including 4 ledger invariants each checked against 200 generated trading histories on every push
Strict TypeScript (strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess) with no any
Zero runtime dependencies beyond React; about 68 kB of JavaScript after gzip
whatIGotWrong: My own test had a bug. The first property-test run found a signed-zero (−0) bug in my reversal test. Hand-written example tests would never have hit it.

Tamper-evident is not tamper-proof. Someone with the device could recompute the whole chain. The fingerprint only protects the owner if it is written down somewhere else, which is exactly what the demo above shows.

I assumed two tabs could fork the chain. They cannot, because entry numbers are unique keys and the second save is rejected whole. I only proved that with a test later, and added a clear message plus cross-tab reload.
Browsers can silently clear site storage. The app now asks for persistent storage and tells the owner whether it was granted, but a CSV export is still the real backup.
No sync yet. One device is the source of truth, so losing the phone without an export loses the book.
next: Sync across devices using the existing hash-linked log
Encrypted cloud backup with a PIN-derived key
Inventory by item so cost of goods sold is calculated

projects.name: Travel & Stays
projects.summary: A two-sided marketplace for verified stays and local tours across Nigeria, with guests, hosts and tour guides, Paystack payments in naira, and an admin dashboard.
projects.hardestPart: Two guests can't book the same dates, even in the same second: a Postgres exclusion constraint makes the double booking impossible, and CI proves it with a race of 8 sessions. A booking is only marked paid after the server confirms the exact amount and currency with Paystack (test mode), covered by 11 unit tests.
projects.note: Payments run in Paystack test mode: no real money moves.

caseStudy.problem: Travellers in Nigeria book short stays mostly through WhatsApp and Instagram: they send money to a stranger and hope the apartment exists. Hosts can’t easily prove they are legitimate, take payment in naira, or stop two people booking the same weekend. The brief was a marketplace for travellers, hosts and tour guides where money, dates and identity can be trusted.

decisions.t: Two guests, same weekend, same second
decisions.d: A “is the date free?” check followed by an insert has a race. I moved the guarantee into Postgres with an exclusion constraint on listing and date range, so a double booking is impossible, not merely unlikely.

decisions.t: “The popup said success” is not proof
decisions.d: The Paystack popup runs in the browser, so anyone can fake it. A server-side Edge Function asks Paystack directly and only accepts the payment when the status, the exact amount to the kobo and the NGN currency all match.

decisions.t: Prices come from the server
decisions.d: create_booking reads the nightly price and cleaning fee from the listing and computes nights, fee and total in SQL, then the charge uses exactly that total. A guest can change what they see, not what they pay.

decisions.t: Users can only touch their own rows
decisions.d: Every table has row-level security and writes go through security-definer functions that check the signed-in user, so the rules hold even if someone calls the API directly.

decisions.t: Trust before visibility
decisions.d: ID documents sit in a private bucket only admins can read. A host’s listings show Verified only after admin approval, and any listing can be reported and paused immediately.

results: Live on Vercel with demo data for stays in all 36 states and the FCT, plus tours
The payment decision is a pure function covered by 11 unit tests, including underpaying by one kobo and the wrong currency

CI on every push: lint, production build, the payment tests, and a database job that builds a fresh Postgres 16 from the real migrations and checks overlap, a same-instant race (8 sessions, exactly one winner), row-level security and hold expiry
Payments run in Paystack test mode; shipped with code reviews from the MALhub engineering team
whatIGotWrong: The headline claim had no test. “The database refuses double bookings” was only true by reading the SQL. There is now a CI job that builds Postgres from the real migrations and proves it, including a same-instant race.

Unpaid holds never expired. Each traveller was capped at 3 unpaid holds, but a hold lasted forever. Migration 019 releases unpaid stays after 72 hours and never touches paid ones or one being paid right now.
If a guest closes the tab right after paying, only the browser call confirmed the payment. I wrote a signature-checked Paystack webhook as a second path.
Two of those fixes (hold expiry and the webhook) are in the repo and tested, but not yet switched on for the live demo project. They need the migration run and the function deployed.
Host payouts are not held until check-in, and refunds are recorded for an admin to process by hand. Paystack is in test mode.

projects.name: RedCart
projects.summary: An online store with 103 products, Google sign-in, Paystack checkout, review fraud scoring, an AI shopping assistant, and a second storefront in Next.js reading the store's API.
projects.hardestPart: The AI assistant isn't allowed to guess. Order status and stock come from the database, and policy answers come from real documents through a small retrieval layer. Payments are re-checked against the cart total on the server before an order exists. 98 tests run in CI.

caseStudy.problem: Small electronics sellers in Nigeria run their shops over WhatsApp: prices change in chats, orders get lost, and a customer has to trust a screenshot of a transfer. RedCart gives them a real storefront and order flow, with Paystack for payment and an assistant that answers from the actual catalogue.

decisions.t: Never trust the browser about payments
decisions.d: After Paystack redirects back, the server calls Paystack’s verify endpoint itself and compares the amount and reference with the order before marking anything paid. A customer cannot mark an order paid by editing a request.

decisions.t: No double credit
decisions.d: Referral rewards are paid into wallets inside a database transaction with select_for_update, so two requests at the same moment cannot pay the same reward twice.

decisions.t: An assistant that does not lie
decisions.d: Order status, stock and prices come from the database, not the model. Policy answers are retrieved from real policy documents, the bot must never claim to have added something to the cart or invent a discount, and a script re-runs guardrail and retrieval checks after changes.

decisions.t: Two frontends, one source of truth
decisions.d: A Next.js and TypeScript storefront reads the same catalogue through the Django API, so prices and stock cannot drift between the two.

decisions.t: Fake reviews without punishing real customers
decisions.d: Each review gets a fraud score from signals like near-duplicate text, a burst on one product, brand-new accounts and generic text with an extreme rating. Only high-confidence fraud is hidden; borderline reviews stay public and are flagged for staff.

results: 98 Django tests pass in CI, including new tests for payment verification (wrong amount, replayed reference, failed payment)
Moved from Render to Vercel with a Neon Postgres database
Payments run in Paystack test mode only; no real money moves
whatIGotWrong: The amount-mismatch branch of my payment check had no test. I found that while writing this page and added tests for it, then checked they fail when the check is removed.
Amounts are float naira rounded to two places. That is fine for a demo and wrong for a ledger; Oja Ledger uses whole kobo for exactly this reason.
The payment logic lives inside a view. That made it harder to test than it should have been.
next: Paystack webhooks, so a payment still lands if the customer closes the tab

projects.name: StudyFlow
projects.summary: A study platform with an AI coach that knows each student's courses and deadlines, a CGPA tracker, an attendance tracker for the 75% rule, spaced-repetition flashcards, CBT practice and study groups.
projects.hardestPart: Uploads are judged by their bytes, not their names: a renamed .exe is rejected by its magic bytes. AI output is sanitised before it touches the page, and AI features are rate-limited per user. 168 tests run in CI.
projects.note: Free-tier hosting: the first load after a quiet spell can take up to a minute.

caseStudy.problem: Students juggle courses, deadlines and revision with a mix of notes apps and calendars, and nothing tells them what to study next. StudyFlow puts courses, tasks and study sessions in one place and adds an AI study coach.

decisions.t: The coach works from the student’s own data
decisions.d: The AI coach is given the student’s real courses and tasks, so its suggestions refer to things that exist rather than generic advice.

decisions.t: Say when the AI is not configured
decisions.d: If no AI key is set, the app says so instead of returning a made-up reply.

decisions.t: Everything is scoped to the signed-in user
decisions.d: Every query filters by the current user, and the tests check one student cannot read another’s records.

results: 168 Django tests run in CI on every push (the count in the repo README)
Free-tier hosting: the first request after idle takes about 30 seconds while the server wakes up
whatIGotWrong: The test count is written differently in two places. Small, but it is the kind of inconsistency that costs trust, so it is on my list.
The free-tier cold start makes the first impression slow. A cheap warm-up would help.

projects.name: LogiTrack
projects.summary: Shipment tracking for small delivery businesses: bulk CSV manifest import with row-level validation, a shipment timeline, and a customer tracking page. Runs as a free demo without Redis or S3.
projects.hardestPart: 35 automated tests. Free demo login is shown on the live site.
projects.note: Demo sign-in: username demo, password demo12345 (a public demo account).

caseStudy.problem: Small delivery businesses track parcels in spreadsheets and chat. LogiTrack gives each business its own workspace for shipments, status changes, bulk imports, delivery proof and a public tracking page.

decisions.t: Strict tenant isolation
decisions.d: Each business only sees its own shipments, exports and import results. There are tests for the multi-tenant case and for the import detail page.

decisions.t: Status changes are validated on the server
decisions.d: A shipment can only move along allowed transitions, and a terminal status cannot change again. The same rule applies in the form and on the server.

decisions.t: Idempotent bulk import
decisions.d: A CSV import (up to 5 MB and 5,000 rows) validates row by row, excludes bad rows, and uses the customer reference as an idempotency key so re-uploading does not create duplicates.

decisions.t: One-time recipient links
decisions.d: When a parcel goes out for delivery, the recipient gets a link that expires after seven days and works once. The token is stored hashed.

decisions.t: Safe public tracking
decisions.d: The public tracking page and API leave out delivery proof and other sensitive fields. Proof-of-delivery files are private with signed links that expire after five minutes.

decisions.t: Signed webhooks
decisions.d: Outgoing webhooks are HMAC-signed, must be HTTPS, and failures are logged to a dead-letter record.

results: Around 35 test methods in the repo, covering transitions, tenant isolation, import idempotency, webhook signing, token expiry and rate limiting
The live demo runs in demo mode: no Postgres, Redis or S3, jobs run inline, and data rebuilds on cold start
whatIGotWrong: The live demo is not the production setup. Carrier sync falls back to a simulated model without API keys, and I say so rather than calling it live tracking.
Email invitations only reach recipients once SMTP is configured; the demo uses the console backend.
next: Real carrier integrations: without API keys it uses a deterministic simulated status model, not live carrier data

projects.name: SpendWise
projects.summary: Track your naira budget, savings goals and monthly bills. Sign in with a passkey instead of a password.
projects.hardestPart: 33 automated tests, decimal money maths and WebAuthn passkeys.

caseStudy.problem: Most budgeting apps either connect to your bank or are spreadsheets in disguise. SpendWise is a Naira-first tracker for accounts, transactions, category budgets and savings goals that does not touch a bank connection.

decisions.t: Decimal money, not floats
decisions.d: Balances and budget maths use Python Decimal, with a test for the arithmetic.

decisions.t: Passkeys verified on the server
decisions.d: WebAuthn challenges and signatures are checked server-side, and a regression test makes sure an invalid assertion does not log anyone in.

decisions.t: CSV that is safe to open
decisions.d: Export escapes cells that start with =, +, - or @ so a spreadsheet cannot run them as formulas. Import previews rows, flags likely duplicates and skips malformed ones.

decisions.t: Honest projection
decisions.d: The 90-day view is based on recent average net cash flow and is labelled indicative, not a forecast.

decisions.t: No faked AI
decisions.d: The money coach uses the signed-in user’s real data and says so when the AI key is missing or the provider fails.

results: Around 34 test methods covering ownership, decimal maths, budgets, CSV import/export, passkeys and the coach endpoints
Privacy mode only blurs amounts in the browser; it is a display feature, not encryption
whatIGotWrong: Privacy mode can look like a security feature. It is not one, and the README says so.
The README describes more features than I have written about tests for. The test list above is what is actually covered.
